purpose: Execution of chapters 1, 4 and 5 of the UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts (2016 edition): general provisions (freedom of contract, its binding character, mandatory rules, exclusion or modification by the parties, supplementation of the Principles, good faith and fair dealing, inconsistent behaviour, usages and practices, notice, definitions and computation of time), interpretation of the contract and of the parties' statements, content of the contract, third party rights and conditions. The package is the HUB of the `unidroit.picc*` group: it owns the types for party, contract, obligation, term, notice and the organ of evaluative elements, and the packages of chapters 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8–11 take them by alias. The primary §194 anchor is the English black-letter text (an official language of the instrument). The list of questions and boundaries is in analysis/questions.json and QUESTIONS.md.
limitations: THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them (Preamble), or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law. They do not replace the rule of a state: article 1.4 expressly preserves mandatory rules, and which rules are mandatory is a question of the applicable law — an input of the case.

THE EVALUATIVE ELEMENTS of chapters 1, 4 and 5 go through the §47.3 judgment channel with the organ `Tribunal`: good faith (1.7), reasonable reliance on an understanding (1.8), unreasonableness of applying a usage (1.9), the closest relationship of a place of business (1.11), the meaning of reasonable persons (4.1, 4.2), ambiguity of a term (4.6), appropriateness of a supplied term (4.8), reasonable efforts (5.1.4), quality no less than average (5.1.6), a manifestly unreasonable determination of price (5.1.7), a reasonable time for notice (5.1.8).
THE ORGAN IS NAMED BY THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF: article 1.11 provides that "court" includes an arbitral tribunal. `authority Tribunal` quotes that definition rather than choosing one.

THE EXTENSION FOR AN OFFICIAL HOLIDAY (article 1.12(2)) CARRIES THE PROVISO "unless the circumstances indicate otherwise", WHICH ARTICLE 20(2) OF THE CONVENTION DOES NOT HAVE: there the extension is unconditional. The two rules must not be merged, and the difference is checked by case 04 rather than by a comment.

THE PRINCIPLES HAVE NO CALENDAR AND NO TIME ZONES: which days are non-business days at the place of performance, and the zone of a place of business, are facts of the case. The §86 policy of the package counts calendar days, and the extension is expressed as a rule over those facts (a policy with a roll would require a §85 calendar snapshot inside the package).
CHAPTERS 2, 3, 6, 7 AND 8–11 LIVE IN THE NEIGHBOURING PACKAGES of the `unidroit.picc*` group; the hub holds chapters 1, 4 and 5 and the types that all of them use.

THE LISTS IN ARTICLES 4.3 AND 5.1.5 ARE NOT EXHAUSTIVE ("among other factors"): the rule recognises a circumstance or a factor of a named kind, while other kinds are left to the assessment of the organ and do not enter the model as separate premises.
